solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Boozer: your second Thatcher, maybe

blocks.note: a boozer is a pub, so a bar
one's is the impersonal form of your
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A drinker addresses someone whose second wife might be a Thatcher-like figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Your' is ONE'S in the impersonal sense ('one's own'), and 'second' is just the abbreviation S, not a second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret Thatcher was made a life peer in 1992, so she is an example of a baroness.

clue.text: Bush cutting out pot with airy vacillation

indicators.note: out here means wrong or not in place, so the letters must be rearranged
vacillation is wavering back and forth, suggesting the letters shift about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dig at President Bush cutting out marijuana with a light-headed indecisiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the US president and 'pot' like cannabis; the bush is a garden shrub being clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Topiary is the art of clipping shrubs into ornamental shapes, so it is cutting a bush.

clue.text: Be glad to get healthy climax-free orgasm

indicators.note: free of its climax means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: well means in good health
come is slang for an orgasm

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about being pleased with a healthy but unfinished sexual experience.
explanation.walkthrough: The climax that is removed belongs to 'healthy', whose last letter goes, not to the orgasm.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome something is to receive it gladly, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: ( 28ac.) Stupid shag's over, chief

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, an idiot; the clue word is an adjective

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: bonk and shag are both British slang for sex
a chief is the head of something

explanation.surface: Someone is told off as stupid now the sex is over.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's in 'shag's' is the link 'is'. Knobhead is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A knobhead is a crude British insult for a stupid person, so it stands for someone stupid.

clue.text: Drink, Lord Prescott's third knocked off with a gesture

indicators.note: third points to the letter in third position of the named word
knocked off means removed, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
the third letter of Prescott
a nod is a gesture of the head

explanation.surface: John Prescott, now a lord, knocks back a drink with a nod.
explanation.walkthrough: John Prescott, former Deputy Prime Minister, did become Lord Prescott, which makes 'Lord Prescott' read as one name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pernod is a French aniseed-flavoured spirit, so it is a brand of drink.

clue.text: see 14ac.
Merkel's OK with Putin's dismissal "My! Finally forgotten the lady's name"

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letter of the word before it
something forgotten is left out, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: ja is German for yes, as Angela Merkel would say
nyet is Russian for no
the last letter of My

explanation.surface: German and Russian leaders trade yes and no while someone fails to recall a woman's name.
explanation.walkthrough: The Y of NYET goes, leaving NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet is a common female first name, so it is one example of a lady's name.

clue.text: Brown & co. once given a large sum surplus; Brown's tip: "Chaps, start to tremble"

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its end letter
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: G, a grand, is a thousand pounds
a surplus is something left over
the final letter of Brown
chaps are men
the first letter of tremble

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown's former administration is handed a big surplus and tells his men to quake.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was UK Prime Minister until 2010; 'once' marks that his team is no longer in office.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown led the Labour administration, so he and his colleagues formed the ruling body of the day.

clue.text: Nuts mangled about the time you expect to land an infectious disease

indicators.note: mangled means crushed out of shape, so the letters are scrambled
about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
ETA is the estimated time of arrival

explanation.surface: Crushed nuts at about landing time might give you a nasty bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The time you expect' leads to ETA, the airline's estimated time of arrival, which is why 'to land' follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetanus is a bacterial infection caught through wounds, causing lockjaw.

clue.text: A complete failure performed an after-dinner function

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective, finished or failed

blocks.note: first meaning: finished, no longer successful
second meaning: did the dishes after a meal

explanation.surface: An after-dinner speaker's turn has flopped completely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After-dinner function' suggests a speech; the function is the washing-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A washed-up person is finished and failed, and to wash up is the British phrase for doing the dishes.

clue.text: Hitler follower: first and last to break one in corruptly

indicators.note: breaking into something means going inside it
corruptly means in a debased, altered way, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A Nazi sympathiser is told to break in a recruit by corrupt means.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First and last' is the alphabet's A and Z, not letters of a clue word.
explanation.definitionFit: A neo-Nazi is a modern adherent of Nazism, so a later follower of Hitler.

clue.text: Cameron, Clegg etc. just for display purposes?

blocks.note: first meaning: the senior ministers of the government
second meaning: a piece of furniture for showing things off

explanation.walkthrough: The jibe is that the coalition ministers are mere ornaments; the question mark flags the furniture sense.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cameron and Nick Clegg sat in the ruling ministerial body, and a display case with glass doors shares the name.

clue.text: Memoir of ex-minister who played gooseberry to a homosexual couple?

definitions.text: who played gooseberry to a homosexual couple?

blocks.note: first meaning: the title of Peter Mandelson's 2010 memoir

blocks.clueFragment: who played gooseberry to a homosexual couple?
blocks.note: second meaning: an extra man tagging along with two men

explanation.walkthrough: To play gooseberry is British for being the unwanted third person with a couple; with two men, that person is one more man.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandelson's autobiography bears this title, and the phrase literally describes a male intruder on a male pair.

clue.text: United recently: "debut scorer of a more innocent age"

definitions.note: the answer is a noun or adjective for someone just married

definitions.text: debut scorer of a more innocent age

blocks.note: first meaning: just joined in marriage

blocks.clueFragment: debut scorer of a more innocent age
blocks.note: second meaning: in chaster times, a bride or groom had sex for the first time on the wedding night

explanation.walkthrough: 'United' and 'scorer' suggest Manchester United and a goal on a player's debut; the score is sexual.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly-wed has just been joined in marriage, and in an age of waiting until the wedding was a first-time lover.

clue.text: (& 6ac.) Name in judo wrestling associated with one skirt-chaser

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
wrestling twists and throws bodies about, so the letters are tumbled

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
taken as written
an means one

explanation.surface: A judo wrestler gets linked with a notorious womaniser.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter for 'Name' goes inside 'judo', and the whole is then scrambled before AN is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Don Juan is the legendary seducer of women, so his name is used for any womaniser.

clue.text: Bloke penetrating you: "OK to score?"

indicators.note: penetrating means entering, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: Sid stands for any ordinary bloke
one is the impersonal you

explanation.surface: A man asks his partner during sex whether he can finish.
explanation.walkthrough: The bedroom surface hides football: onside means not offside, so a goal may stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A football player who is onside is in a legal position, so a goal scored then is allowed.

clue.text: Taking Clegg's lead, "this, or chaos!" – it won't fly

indicators.note: a lead goes in front, so the opening letter of the name is taken
chaos is utter disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the first letter of Clegg
taken as written

explanation.surface: Following Nick Clegg's lead offers a choice between this or chaos, a plan that won't fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It won't fly' reads as dismissing a plan, but it is the definition: a flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich is the largest flightless bird, so it is a thing that cannot fly.

clue.text: Boring personal updates of non-drinkers about "piss"

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

blocks.note: a TT, a teetotaller, does not drink alcohol
wee is a gentler word for urine

explanation.surface: Teetotallers' dull social posts are all about urination.
explanation.walkthrough: TT, short for teetotal, is a British label for someone who never drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweets are short posts on Twitter, often mundane personal news.

clue.text: Recognised, taking drugs and pissed

blocks.note: E is ecstasy, so ES are ecstasy tablets
pissed down is slang for rained heavily, as did teemed

explanation.surface: Someone is spotted high on drugs and drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pissed' looks like British slang for drunk, but the sense used is the rain: it pissed down, it teemed.
explanation.definitionFit: An esteemed person is held in respect, acknowledged for their merit.

clue.text: Like Stephen Fry before devouring United's no.1, say, French-style

indicators.note: devouring means swallowing, so the outer piece takes the others inside
the number one letter is the first one of the word

blocks.note: ere is an old word for before
the first letter of United
dit is French for says or said

explanation.surface: Stephen Fry, before he gobbles a United star, speaks in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Stephen Fry is the British actor and broadcaster famed for his learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Fry is known for his wide knowledge, so he is a byword for being learned.

clue.text: Cyclops's rest over: end of Jimmy Riddle

indicators.note: over means turned about, so these letters are rearranged
end of takes the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: the setter speaking of themself says my
taken as written
the last letter of Jimmy

explanation.surface: Cyclops's break is over and it's time for a jimmy riddle.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy riddle is rhyming slang for piddle, a pee; here 'Riddle' is split off as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzle, something baffling, which is a mystery.

clue.text: (& 22ac.) "Joke" adversary finally intermixed with Tory MPs, twats by which the country is now run

definitions.text: by which the country is now run

indicators.note: finally picks out the closing letters of the words before it
intermixed means mixed together, so all the letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: the last letters of Joke and adversary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A jab at the Tory MPs and their coalition partners now governing the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that in 2010 Britain was run by a coalition, the joke of a two-party arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-party system is government by two dominant parties, and the coalition literally ruled as two parties.

clue.text: Cocaine taken in performing the full Monty, available if needed

indicators.note: taken in means absorbed inside, so this piece sits within the others

blocks.note: a performer is on stage
C is slang shorthand for cocaine
the full Monty means everything, all of it

explanation.surface: A stripper snorts coke before going the full Monty.
explanation.walkthrough: The full Monty is British slang for everything, made famous by the 1997 strip-show film.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor on call is ready to be summoned whenever needed.

clue.text: see 20ac.
Balls covered by belly, hoisted to be discreet

indicators.note: hoisted means lifted up, which in a down answer reads the word bottom to top
in a down answer, covered by places one piece below the other

blocks.note: tum is a childish word for the belly
Ed Balls was a senior Labour politician

explanation.surface: Testicles hidden under a raised paunch, keeping things discreet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is not testicles but Ed Balls, Labour's shadow chancellor of the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted means toned down and subdued, as discreet behaviour is.

clue.text: Fashionable set amidst Conservative line-up wants David's head

indicators.note: a head is at the top, so the first letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: amidst means in
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
a row is a line of things
the first letter of David

explanation.surface: The trendy clique in the Conservative ranks wants David Cameron ousted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wants David's head' sounds like a coup against Cameron, but it only supplies a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The in-crowd is the fashionable clique of the moment.

clue.text: Two arses holding Oxford crew?

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the letters sit inside the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A rude jibe that the Oxford boat crew are a pair of idiots.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: oars stand for the rowers who wield them.
explanation.definitionFit: Oarsmen in the Boat Race are called oars, so the Oxford crew is made of them.

clue.text: Faction of eventual Labour leaders into mugging

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the words named
into means going inside, so the letters enter the next piece

blocks.note: the first letter of Labour
the first letter of eventual
a mugging is a theft by force

explanation.surface: A wing of future Labour leaders gets caught up in a mugging.
explanation.walkthrough: The two initials are placed Labour's first: 'eventual' hints its letter comes later.
explanation.definitionFit: The Left is the socialist wing of a party such as Labour, a faction within it.

clue.text: Clinton, length whipped out, has word: "Time for some education"

indicators.note: whipped out means pulled away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Hillary Clinton, the American politician
L is the abbreviation for length
a term is a word

explanation.surface: A Clinton sex scandal has a lesson in it, with a lewd 'length whipped out'.
explanation.walkthrough: One L of her first name goes. Hilary term is the spring term at Oxford and some other British universities.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary term is a university teaching period, so it is a time when education happens.
